A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same work. All 13 pages, including equations, references and the supplementary proof, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical proofs and a closed-form Gaussian consumption–income example in Section 4. Neither the main text nor the appendix reports experiments, simulations, user studies or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains the analytical example and theoretical supplement without adding empirical results. Section 4's numerical quantities are derived analytically rather than estimated from data or simulations.

M1.justification: The shift–scale intervention mechanism and shared-noise twin-SCM construction in Section 2 are unchanged. No algorithm or model component is revised.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or benchmarks. Both retain the same analytical consumption–income example in Section 4.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline methods. The cited counterfactual frameworks remain background references.

E3.justification: Neither version introduces an empirical evaluation protocol. Section 4 retains the same model coefficients, Gaussian noise covariance and intervention parameters, α = 0.8 and β = 1.0.

E4.justification: The worked example is unchanged. Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures. Proposition 2's revised concentration bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Section 4's analytical numerical outcomes are identical, including factual mean (1.5625, 1.125), interventional mean (2.024, 2.048), and correlations 0.75 and approximately 0.69. No empirical results are added or revised.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 corrects the twin solution map's Lipschitz constant from 1/(1−κ) to √2/(1−κ), doubling the sub-Gaussian proxy and changing the exponential bound's denominator from 2(1−κ)^−2σ² to 4(1−κ)^−2σ². Remark 2 correspondingly adds factors 2^(1/p) to the Lipschitz constant and 2^(2/p) to the proxy. These are localized mathematical corrections; the assumptions and other proofs, including the supplementary theorem, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about simplicity under contraction, solvability under shift–scale interventions, closure under composition and sub-Gaussian concentration.

C2.justification: The interpretations of cyclic equilibria and the worked example are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning global contraction, Gaussian noise, coordinate domains, practical certification and intervention classes.

D1.justification: No implementation details, computational resources, hyperparameters or code/data access information are added or revised. The analytical example's technical specification is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the distinction between the proposed sufficient conditions and existing closure results for simple SCMs.

P1.justification: The supplement is renumbered from A/A.1 to 7/7.1, with the corresponding cross-reference updated in Section 2.2. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Reference entries have increased vertical spacing on page 11, and the corrected equations produce minor reflow on page 8. The theorem-box styling remains unchanged, and neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the missing factors arising from the twin SCM's two copies sharing exogenous noise. This repairs an overly strong quantitative concentration guarantee in Proposition 2 and Remark 2 while preserving their qualitative conclusions. The correction improves mathematical reliability within a limited part of the otherwise unchanged paper.
